merger_description:
Boutique Capital Pty Ltd, as trustee for the Royal Foods Unit Trust (**Boutique**), proposes to acquire 22.32% of the issued share capital in Royal Foods Aust Pty Ltd (**Royal Foods**) (the **Acquisition**).

Boutique is an independent professional trustee and Australian financial services licensee that acts as trustee and administrator for trusts operated by independent investment managers. It holds no beneficial interest in the Royal Foods Unit Trust or its assets.

Boutique is a related entity of 29 North Pty Ltd (**29 North**), which is an existing shareholder of Royal Foods. 29 North is a private investment and funds management business that acquires and manages interests in operating businesses across a range of sectors. These investments are either held through 29 North or other unit trusts established to hold those investments. 29 North is the exclusive investment manager of the Royal Foods Unit Trust under an investment management agreement and is a corporate authorised representative of Boutique.

Royal Foods supplies food products to both the food service sector and the retail supermarket industry in Australia.

29 North currently owns 10% of the issued share capital in Royal Foods. As a result of the Acquisition, 29 North and Boutique will together hold approximately 33% of the shares on issue in Royal Foods.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationship between 29 North (and its connected entities)
and Royal Foods in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
